answer_text:
Since no parameter interval is specified, we assume \(C\) is traced once over a full period, say \(0 \le t \le 2\pi\).

For a scalar line integral,

\[
\int_C x\,ds=\int_a^b x(t)\,\|\mathbf r'(t)\|\,dt.
\]

The parametrization is

\[
\mathbf r(t)=\left(\frac34\sin(2t),\ \cos^3 t,\ \sin^3 t\right).
\]

Differentiate:

\[
\mathbf r'(t)=
\left(
\frac32\cos(2t),\ -3\cos^2 t\sin t,\ 3\sin^2 t\cos t
\right).
\]

Then

\[
\|\mathbf r'(t)\|^2
=
\frac94\cos^2(2t)+9\cos^4t\sin^2t+9\sin^4t\cos^2t.
\]

Factor the last two terms:

\[
9\cos^4t\sin^2t+9\sin^4t\cos^2t
=
9\sin^2t\cos^2t(\cos^2t+\sin^2t)
=
9\sin^2t\cos^2t.
\]

Using \(\sin(2t)=2\sin t\cos t\),

\[
9\sin^2t\cos^2t=\frac94\sin^2(2t).
\]

Thus

\[
\|\mathbf r'(t)\|^2
=
\frac94\cos^2(2t)+\frac94\sin^2(2t)
=
\frac94.
\]

So

\[
ds=\|\mathbf r'(t)\|\,dt=\frac32\,dt.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\int_C x\,ds
=
\int_0^{2\pi}
\left(\frac34\sin(2t)\right)\left(\frac32\right)dt
=
\frac98\int_0^{2\pi}\sin(2t)\,dt.
\]

Since \(\sin(2t)\) integrates to zero over a full period,

\[
\int_0^{2\pi}\sin(2t)\,dt=0.
\]

Hence,

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
